subject: business-studies
title: Cash Flow Stretch Adventure
welcome_lead: Exam-style stretch. Evaluate solutions to a cash crisis and judge a forecast's reliability.
meta_desc: GCSE Business Studies stretch — evaluating cash-flow solutions and forecast reliability.
final_note: You can evaluate cash-flow solutions, judge a forecast's reliability and recommend with reasoning.

concepts.def: Ability to pay short-term debts with cash
Selling unpaid invoices to a third party
How long buyers have to pay invoices
Owed money the firm can't collect
How accurate a forecast is likely to be
Plan or buffer for unexpected events

walkthroughs.body_html:
Compare cost vs speed vs side-effects.

Overdrafts: fast but interest. Factoring: instant cash but you receive less. Cutting marketing: cheap but hurts future sales.

Forecasts are predictions — and can be wrong.

They depend on assumed sales, costs, and timing. New firms have especially unreliable forecasts.

Quote the figures, explain the knock-on effects across months, then recommend a remedy that suits the business.

Avoid generic advice — match the action to the actual cause of the cash gap.

mcqs.q: Which is a DRAWBACK of using an overdraft?
options: Repayment can be demanded at any time
